title: Read the assertions of the five guards PR #77 marked NOT REACHED, classify them by failure direction, and pin what is measurably unreached
objective: PR #77 classified 17 repository-owned guards and deliberately marked five NOT REACHED: it read their names, locations and purpose but NOT their assertions. This slice reads the assertions, classifies each by failure direction (A = wrongly reject, B = wrongly accept), and establishes reachability by MUTATION rather than by coverage. Where a guard does not bite, the hole is REPORTED and NOT repaired. Where a guard does bite, tests are added only to pin behaviour that already exists.
what_this_slice_is_not: It is not a repair. No guard's matching rule, admission criterion, accept set or reject set is changed. apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py, apps/api/app/ingest/fetch.py, apps/api/app/ingest/trust.py, apps/api/app/publish/gate.py, apps/api/app/publish/publisher.py, apps/api/app/ingest/reconcile.py and scripts/refresh_secrets_baseline.py are all byte-identical to base, verified by git blob hash.
It does not mark any feature passing. agent-state/feature_list.json is untouched (blob 154de1fef2ba).
It does not touch .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/check_urls.py, tests/unit/test_url_allowlist.py, .secrets.baseline, or either lockfile.
No npm install / i / update / audit fix was run. No Node gate was executed at all (see not_verified).

the_five_guards_as_named_by_pr_77.note: PR #77's inventory row 16 names the runtime staleness gate as app/ingest/trust.py. That file contains NO staleness logic; it is the community/official trust separation boundary. The runtime staleness gate is assess_staleness in app/ingest/reconcile.py, consumed by publisher._build_conditions. Both were audited rather than choosing between them, because classifying from a name is the precise error this slice exists to attack.
the_five_guards_as_named_by_pr_77.4_runtime_staleness_gate: app/ingest/reconcile.py assess_staleness + publisher._build_conditions (NOT trust.py); trust.py audited separately

method.primary_instrument: MUTATION, not name-grep and not coverage. A name-grep answers 'who calls this symbol', not 'what guards this behaviour'; executed-and-unasserted is worse than never-executed because coverage reports it green while deleting the guard fails no test.
method.every_mutation_restores_the_original_def: No mutation deletes an argument or breaks arity. Each one re-opens the specific hole its guard exists to close, and the killing test node ids are recorded so a kill by a DIFFERENT guard is never accepted as evidence for the one under test.
method.baseline_shown_to_have_executed: Round 1: exit 0, 3006 collected, 3006 passed, recorded BEFORE any edit. Round 2 (after the new tests): exit 0, 3031 collected, 3031 passed. pytest exit 5 is treated as NOTHING COLLECTED and aborts the run; a run collecting 0 is never read as a pass.
method.anchor_preflight: Every mutation's search text is asserted to match EXACTLY ONCE before it is applied; a missing anchor ABORTS, because an unapplied mutation reads exactly like a surviving one. 22 of 22 (round 1) and 9 of 9 (round 2) matched exactly once.
method.restoration_proved: Every target file's git blob hash is compared before and after; all 31 mutations restored byte-exact, and git status is clean of production-file changes.
method.structure_over_phrase: The conflicting_assertion branch question was settled by temporarily tagging the two detail strings and driving both input shapes, and by an ast walk over _apply_assertions -- not by counting tokens.
environment_precondition_asserted_not_an: Own PostgreSQL: container fta-guardaudit-pg, volume fta-guardaudit-pgdata, port 55440 probed free before use, bound to 127.0.0.1, seeded separately from any other stack.
Reachability asserted by executing 'select version()' from the venv python and reading a bare exit code, not by reading a docker status line.

The integration suite is asserted to have RUN rather than skipped: 294 integration tests passed; without DATABASE_URL every one of them skips, and a skipped suite would have read as a KILL for every staleness mutation.

in_scope: Read and quote the assertions of all five guards plus trust.py.
Classify each by failure direction and establish reachability by mutation.
ADD tests that pin CURRENT behaviour where a mutation proved a guard does not bite.
Report, and do not repair, any guard that does not bite.
out_of_scope: Changing what any guard matches, accepts or rejects. Three of the five sit in mandatory Level-2 categories (provider adapters and evidence extraction; publication decisions) and one is a security boundary.
Removing the structurally dead second conflicting_assertion branch in _apply_assertions. It is reported. Deleting a refusal from an evidence-extraction path is an owner decision.
Any Node-side gate, for the reason recorded in not_verified.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five guards has its assertion QUOTED, a failure direction assigned from that assertion rather than from its name, and a REACHED / NOT REACHED verdict established by mutation with the killing test named.
Every guard reported as reached names at least one test that goes red when its defect is restored.
Every guard reported as NOT reached survived a defect-restoring mutation against the whole tree, with the baseline shown green and non-empty first.
Each added test file asserts BOTH directions: a refusing arm and a permitting arm differing in exactly one input, so it cannot pass against code that refuses everything.
Every added test is shown to BITE by re-running the mutation it was written for and observing it go from SURVIVED to KILLED, naming the killing test.
No production file changes. Byte-identity proved by git blob hash.
Errors made during the slice are reported as prominently as the verdict.

verification_method.database: Own PostgreSQL 16, container fta-guardaudit-pg, volume fta-guardaudit-pgdata, host port 55440 (probed free; the repo default 5432 and the previously used 55432 were both already allocated). Removed with exact-name ^...$ filters at end of slice, because Docker's default filter is a SUBSTRING match.
commands: python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"   (scripts/bootstrap-dev.ps1 NOT used: it runs npm install, which is forbidden here)
.venv/Scripts/python -m alembic upgrade head   (against the audit database only)
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests -q -p no:randomly   (whole-tree selector used for every mutation)

migration_and_data_implications: None. No schema change, no migration, no production write. The audit database is created, migrated and destroyed inside the slice.

security_privacy_portability_z0.security: apps/api/app/ingest/fetch.py is a security boundary and was NOT modified. Its guards were exercised by mutation only, with every mutation restored byte-exact. No security check was weakened, suppressed or relaxed; no allowlist entry was added. Where a mutation survived, the finding is reported rather than repaired.
security_privacy_portability_z0.portability: No dependency added or changed. Neither lockfile touched.
security_privacy_portability_z0.z0: Material. Two of the guards audited stand directly between an unsupported free claim and publication: the provider assertion floor (an unpinned claim must never become a fact) and the publication gate's fresh hard condition (a stale claim must never auto-publish). Both were proved to bite. The one publication-side hole found -- a source with NO snapshot at all being reportable as fresh -- is the unknown-treated-as-verified shape, and is now pinned by test at its current fail-closed value.

regression_risks: The added tests are pure additions; no existing test was modified or weakened.

tests/unit/test_secrets_refresher.py drives scripts/refresh_secrets_baseline.py's main() against a TEMPORARY root and stubs run_scan, so detect-secrets is never invoked and the committed .secrets.baseline is never read or written. The redirection is asserted inside the fixture, not assumed.
The new test files contain no 40-hex literal; every digest is computed at run time, so they introduce no new detect-secrets finding and cannot make the committed baseline stale.
required_evaluation_level_reason: The audit reads and exercises guards in three mandatory Level-2 categories (provider adapters and evidence extraction; publication decisions; security boundaries). No behaviour is changed, but the CLAIMS made about those guards' reachability are exactly the kind of claim that must be independently checked, and two of the added test files sit against Level-2 code.
hard_rules_acknowledged: No feature marked passing; agent-state/feature_list.json untouched.
agent-state/progress.md appended to only, proved by raw byte-prefix comparison plus a flipped-byte negative control.
agent-state/current_contract.json taken wholesale (single-slot, no carry-forward since PR #106).
Own PostgreSQL on a probed-free port; container and volume removed and named in the report using exact-name ^...$ filters.
Rebased on main before pushing if main moved, because a conflicting PR is never dispatched to CI and an absent signal reads exactly like a green one.
not_verified: NODE-SIDE GATES: RETIRED by CI. I did not run them locally because this machine npm registry is an internal package feed and npm ci/install could write internal resolved URLs into a lockfile -- the exact disclosure scripts/check_urls.py exists to catch, in a public repository. CI run 33461023775 then ran them: Node format and lint PASS, Web type-check tests and build PASS. Verified, but not by me.

CI ITSELF: RETIRED. Observed on the draft PR, run 33461023775, all six checks green (Python lint/format/tests 2m9s, Node format and lint, Web type-check/tests/build, Secret scan, Dependency audit, GitGuardian). The PR is MERGEABLE, so the run was genuinely dispatched -- a conflicting PR is never dispatched at all and an absent signal reads exactly like a green one.
CI ITSELF: I did not observe a CI run. The verdicts here are from local execution against my own PostgreSQL.

REACHABILITY IN PRODUCTION of the publisher's freshest-is-None branch: I proved the branch is live through the seam an existing unit test already uses, and pinned it. I did NOT establish whether the real pipeline can produce a candidate for a source with zero snapshots. If it cannot, the branch is a fail-closed default for an unreachable state, which is still correct and still worth pinning.

THE PERMIT DIRECTION OF THE REFRESHER AGAINST REAL detect-secrets: the added tests stub run_scan. They prove the wrapper's REACTION to a scan result, not that detect-secrets produces the results modelled. The four historical corruption shapes those models are drawn from are the ones already recorded in tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py.

THE IPv4-MAPPED UNMASK in address_block_reason: NOT classifiable by mutation on this interpreter. My mutation was EQUIVALENT, not defect-restoring -- CPython's ipaddress already delegates mapped addresses internally, so removing the explicit unmask changes neither the verdict nor the reason string for ::ffff:127.0.0.1, ::ffff:10.0.0.1, ::ffff:8.8.8.8 or ::ffff:1.1.1.1 (all four probed). Its survival is therefore evidence about my instrument, not about the tests.
